notes: How this part was researched: the session's web-search allowance was already used up, so every page was opened directly with the kit's honest User-Agent: campaign sites, each county's, city's and school district's own site, party units' own sites (the Republican units through the state party's 'Find Your Local Republicans' directory, the DFL through its endorsed list), the University of Minnesota's election archive, and local newspapers' own site searches (hometownsource.com, the Mankato Free Press, the Forum Communications papers).

Which candidates had filed a campaign website was read from a scratch copy of the database on which the project's own filed-websites step had already been run (the real database has no websites table yet and was only read). Fourteen of the thirty filed one. A website is recorded here only where the site itself was opened and names the candidate and the office. The address for Christopher Albers was found by trying it; no website is filed for him.

Campaign sites that could not be read, so no website and no words are recorded from them: shawnsavela.com and supina4eagan.com (which leads to mikesupina.com) each showed this script a bot check; votejennifermcpherson67a.com answers 503 with its host's holding page ('If you are the owner of this site, please contact Campaign Partner Support'); tedforstillwater.com answers 500 with a WordPress 'critical error' page; quayleforedina.com answered 429 (too many requests) on each of three tries; judgeluismorales.com shows only 'Launching Soon'. hoffmanforsheriff.com exists and also shows only 'Launching Soon', naming nobody, so it is not recorded for Mike Hoffman. The 8th Congressional District Republicans' page links Shawn Savela's name to shawnsavela.com, and the Sun Current's voter's guide prints Sarah Quayle's own answer 'Visit quayleforedina.com'.

Three filed addresses answer only with www in front: wesenbergforsenate.com without it fails its certificate check (the certificate is for another name), and mnkarlolson.org and wrightformn.org without it have no address at all. The pages were read at the www addresses given here.

Government sites not read: the City of Eagan's site (cityofeagan.com) showed this script a bot check, so Mike Supina has no official page here and his council service rests on Sun Thisweek. The Governor's newsroom on mn.gov answered with a CAPTCHA page on the first request and was not asked again, and the Judicial Branch's site was not requested at all (another part found it refuses scripts), so neither judge has an official page and their appointments rest on newspapers. Neither story says the judge serves today, so the end of each judgeship is left blank. The Austin Daily Herald's site answered 403.

Party endorsements: the Senate District 46 Republicans' own home page lists Kayla Wright and Karl Olson as endorsed, and the Minnesota DFL's list names Vanessa Davenport. Nathan Wesenberg's own site says he is endorsed by Senate District 10, but no party unit's page saying so was found: the state party's directory gives no site for a Senate District 10 or Morrison County unit, the address the Benton County Republicans link for 'SD10' (morrisoncountygop.com) has no address, and the pages opened on the Crow Wing, Aitkin and Kanabec units' sites name no endorsed legislative candidates. The 8th Congressional District Republicans' '2026 Candidates' page lists 'SD 10 - Nathan Wesenberg' and 'HD 8B - Shawn Savela' but does not call the list endorsements, so it is not recorded as one. The St. Louis County Republicans' post-primary page does not name Savela, and the page the state party's directory gives for the Senate District 8 Republicans is on a social network. The home pages of the local DFL units' sites that were opened (Senate Districts 52, 39, 33 and 55) show no endorsements for the nonpartisan city and school races in this part.

Shawn Savela's 2024 run is from the Minnesota Historical Election Archive (University of Minnesota Libraries), a university archive of official returns that cites the State Canvassing Report; it is labelled secondary for the second reader to judge, as in other parts. The archive's page for him also shows a birth date without naming a source for it; it was not taken. The archive has no page for Kayla Wright, Karl Olson, Vanessa Davenport or Jennifer McPherson.
No birth year is recorded for anyone. Two of the newspaper stories cited here give an age rather than a year (for Mike Supina and Jessica Hatanpa); an age is not a birth year, so nothing was taken.

Offices are elected or appointed seats on public bodies only. What the candidates' own pages and the news stories say of paid work, careers, military service, schooling and household is not recorded, and seats on private groups' boards were left out. One case for the second reader to judge: a staff post in county emergency management that one candidate's own site describes as part of a sheriff's office job was treated as a job. Tonja West-Hafner's site also lists city task forces of 2006 to 2018 that are not recorded one by one, and Sarah Quayle's one entry is a seat on a school district committee, labelled as such.

Names: the Sun Thisweek story on the First District appointment writes Luis Rangel Morales and our list writes Luis Morales (his filed address is judgeluismorales.com); the City of Breckenridge writes Russ Wilson and Russell Wilson and our list writes Russel E Wilson; the campaign site for Faribault County Sheriff writes Chris Albers and our list writes Christopher Albers.

Julie Clark: the City of Mounds View's City Council Directory, given as her official page, also prints council members' home addresses and telephone numbers; nothing of that was recorded, and the second reader may prefer to leave the link out. Her start is left blank because the city's tenure list shows her from the 2024 row, after a special election on 11/07/2023, without the day she took the seat.

Wilkin County's own County Board page lists Jonathan Green as the 2nd District commissioner (2023-2026); neither candidate for that seat on our list holds it. Proctor's School Board page does not list Anna Carlson among its members, and Glencoe-Silver Lake's does not list Kevin Kuester today.
Nothing citable was found for Jennifer McPherson and Anna Carlson: each has a name others share, and no page read ties either to her 2026 race beyond the list itself.

verifier_notes: Every address in the file was opened again on 2026-10-02 with the kit's honest User-Agent; all answered, and the recorded words were found on each page. The Mounds View tenure list (a PDF) was read with the kit's own PDF reader.

Corrected wording: Shawn Savela's 2024 primary is not on the cited general-election page, so it was dropped from the entry; the Davenport site's About page is now named by its address; the West Central Tribune story's headline is given as the page prints it, and a second story cited without an address was dropped; the Stillwater profile's words are quoted as printed (it writes Teddy Kozlowski).
